daily.title: Protein prices bite as food inflation squeezes Indian households
daily.summary: Food inflation more than doubles since April, with prices of proteins such as milk, pulses, meats and eggs soaring. New Delhi: Grocery bills are getting heavier for Indian households, and putting enough protein on the table is becoming increasingly expensive. From key pulses and meat to fish and eggs, the prices of everyday protein sources are rising sharply, squeezing family budgets and making a balanced diet harder to afford, particularly for lower-income households.

daily.title: Unallocated Crop Insurance Premium Not Taxable Before Risk Commences: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi upholds deletion of additions on crop insurance premiums, corpus interest and lower TDS, while remanding disputed prior period expenses. Summary: The Delhi Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal disposed of six appeals involving Agriculture Insurance Company of India for assessment years 2020-21 to 2023-24, taking AY 2020-21 as the lead year. The general insurance company, engaged particularly in crop insurance, had returned income of ₹244.93 crore for AY 2020-21, against assessed income of ₹710.63 crore. The CIT(A) deleted several additions but sustained the prior period expenditure disallowance.

daily.title: Winding-Up Petition Dismissed Amid Existing SEBI Recovery Proceedings: NCLT Indore
daily.summary: NCLT rejects Sai Prakash Properties winding-up plea, citing existing SEBI recovery proceedings and Supreme Court-supervised investor claims process. Summary : The National Company Law Tribunal, Indore Bench, dismissed a petition seeking the winding up of Sai Prakash Properties Development Limited under Sections 271 to 273 of the Companies Act, 2013 , holding that a separate liquidation proceeding was unnecessary when SEBI had already initiated regulatory action and the Supreme Court had established a supervised mechanism for resolving investor claims.

daily.title: NCLT Orders Meeting of 896 Unsecured Creditors in Sonepar India Merger

Summary : The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), New Delhi Bench, Court-VI, in the matter of the proposed amalgamation of NM Automation & Control Private Limited with Sonepar India Private Limited , held that the requirement of convening a meeting of unsecured creditors could not be dispensed with merely because the transferor company was a wholly owned subsidiary of the transferee company and the proposed merger was stated to have no adverse effect on creditors.

daily.title: CBIC Proposes Changes to Section 16 and New Section 16A to Protect Genuine ITC Claims
daily.summary: CBIC proposes changes to Section 16 & new Section 16A to protect genuine ITC claims, aiming to prevent penalising recipients for supplier defaults. The proposal seeks to bring greater clarity to ITC eligibility and ensure that bona fide recipients are not penalised merely because of defaults committed by suppliers or other persons in the supply chain. At the same time, it aims to prevent taxpayers knowingly involved in fraudulent transactions from claiming ITC. The proposals form part of an agenda note prepared by the GST Policy Wing of CBIC following deliberations at the 57th GST Council meeting.

daily.title: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
daily.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said his government was in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur in Hooghly district, a day after Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced Ashok Leyland would set up a truck manufacturing plant there. Singur was the site of Tata Motors' Nano small-car factory, for which the then Left Front government acquired around 997 acres in 2006. The acquisition triggered a prolonged farmers' agitation led by Mamata Banerjee, following which Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008.

daily.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has issued Notification No. 95/2026-Customs (N.T.) dated The notification has been issued in exercise of the powers conferred under clauses (b) and (c) of Section 7(1) of the Customs Act, 1962 . daily.title: CBIC Issues Detailed Guidelines for Implementation of Diamond Imprest Authorisation Scheme: Clarifies 12-Month Import Validity, 18-Month Export Obligation, 10% Value Addition and Customs Duty Exemption
daily.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has issued Circular No. 48/2026-Customs dated November 20, The Circular has been issued to ensure uniform implementation of the Scheme by Customs field formations and to clarify the eligibility conditions, import restrictions, export obligations, documentation requirements, security arrangements and procedures for regularisation of defaults. The Scheme provides for duty-exempt imports of eligible natural cut and polished diamonds against a prescribed obligation to undertake physical exports of natural cut and polished diamonds with minimum value addition.
